title: Towards welfare-oriented recommendations in activity-travel behavior
abstract: arXiv:2608.16922v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While mainstream recommender systems (RS) rely on diverse heuristics to rank alternatives, they generally lack a principled account of user welfare (i.e., whether accepting the recommendation will leave the user better off than other alternatives). The problem is particularly acute in activity-based travel behavior, where users incur costs they cannot recoup (i.e., energy, time) regardless of eventual satisfaction. As a result, existing systems may recommend options based on popularity or collaborative filtering, but may still leave users worse off than nearby or self-selected alternatives. We address this gap by introducing a welfare-oriented framework for activity recommendation that evaluates suggestions in terms of net utility, defined as experienced benefit minus travel costs. translated_title: 面向福利导向的活动-出行行为推荐
translated_abstract: 虽然主流推荐系统（RS）依赖多种启发式方法来对备选项进行排序，但它们通常缺乏对用户福利的原则性考量（即，接受推荐是否会让用户比选择其他备选项更有利）。这一问题在基于活动的出行行为中尤为突出，因为用户无论最终是否满意，都会承担无法收回的成本（如能源、时间）。因此，现有系统可能基于流行度或协同过滤来推荐选项，但仍可能让用户比选择邻近或自选的备选项更差。我们通过引入一个面向福利的活动推荐框架来解决这一差距，该框架以净效用（定义为体验收益减去出行成本）来评估建议。具体而言，我们形式化了两个操作性决策标准：正效用概率（PUP）仅在净效用非负的概率较高时进行推荐。
tldr: 本文提出一个面向福利的活动推荐框架，通过净效用（体验收益减去出行成本）和正效用概率标准，确保推荐能真正提升用户福利而非仅依赖流行度或协同过滤。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a welfare-oriented activity recommendation framework that evaluates suggestions via net utility (experienced benefit minus travel costs) and a Positive Utility Probability criterion, ensuring recommendations genuinely improve user welfare beyond popularity or collaborative filtering.
